acts.desc: Ira introduces this week's show, which includes two stories of people who speak up when most people would keep quiet.
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: One day, Joe Lipari had a frustrating encounter with a worker at the Apple Store. And then Joe did what a lot of us would do: He vented. But he vented in a way that ended up having some serious repercussions. Producer Ben Calhoun tells the story.
acts.title: The First Rule of the Apple Store: Don't Talk About the Apple Store

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: For 17 months, New York police officer Adrian Schoolcraft recorded himself and his fellow officers on the job, including their supervisors ordering them to do all sorts of things that police aren't supposed to do. For example, downgrading real crimes into lesser ones, so they wouldn't show up in the crime statistics and make their precinct look bad. Adrian's story first appeared as a five part series in the Village Voice, written by Graham Rayman.
acts.title: Is That a Tape Recorder in Your Pocket, or Are You Just Unhappy to See Me?
